title: Research | Shailesh Kushwaha
text:
My research lies at the intersection of experimental heat transfer, computational fluid dynamics, reduced-order modeling, and scientific machine learning. I develop and investigate thermal management systems through a combination of experimental methods, high-fidelity numerical simulations, and data-driven computational techniques.
My broader objective is to develop accurate and computationally efficient approaches for thermal analysis, prediction, and optimization.

title: Research | Shailesh Kushwaha
text:
1. Experimental Thermal Engineering
My experimental work focuses on the thermal management of electronic systems and the development of experimental facilities for investigating advanced cooling technologies.

Electronics Cooling
During my master’s research, I designed and fabricated an in-house experimental facility for investigating PCM-based heat sinks. The experimental work included different fin configurations and a heat-pipe-coupled three-fin heat sink.
The study investigated the charging and discharging behavior of PCM-based heat sinks and evaluated their thermal performance under different operating conditions. The heat-pipe-coupled configuration demonstrated improved performance compared with the other configurations investigated.
Key areas:

PCM-based heat sinks
Heat pipe-assisted cooling
Thermal performance characterization
Experimental heat transfer
Thermal management of electronic components



Immersion Cooling
I am also developing an in-house experimental facility for single-phase immersion cooling of data center servers, with the aim of investigating alternative cooling strategies for high-density computing systems.

title: About Shailesh Kushwaha | IIT Madras
text:
I am Shailesh Kushwaha, a Ph.D. Research Scholar in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras), where I conduct research under the supervision of Prof. C. Balaji.
My academic and research background is in thermal engineering and thermal management of electronic systems. My work combines experimental investigations with computational modeling and data-driven methods to address challenging heat-transfer problems.
During my research career, I have designed and developed in-house experimental facilities for electronics and data center cooling. I have also developed computational models and used experimental measurements for model validation. Building on this foundation, my doctoral research has expanded toward machine-learning-assisted reduced-order modeling for rapid thermal prediction.
I am particularly interested in developing computational approaches that can bridge the gap between high-fidelity physics-based simulations and fast predictive models. Looking ahead, I am interested in scientific machine learning and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for developing efficient alternatives or complements to conventional CFD.

title: Publications | Shailesh Kushwaha
text:
2026

Reduced order modeling of air-cooled data center using data-driven proper orthogonal decomposition
Authors: Shailesh Kushwaha, Ankith Suresh, C. Balaji
Journal: Applied Thermal Engineering, 303 (2026), 132277
Status: Published
DOI: 10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.132277
Highlights

Developed a data-driven POD-Random Forest reduced-order model for air-cooled data center thermal prediction.
Evaluated POD-RF against POD-LSR and POD-MARS.
Validated the models using 114 independent test cases.
POD-RF achieved an MAE of 0.621 K, RMSE of 0.831 K, and (R^2=0.958).
Reduced online prediction time from approximately 5 hours for CFD to less than 1 second per operating condition.

Highlights

Conducted experimental investigations of PCM-based heat sinks.
Investigated different fin configurations and PCM fill ratios.
Developed a three-fin heat sink coupled with a heat pipe.
The heat-pipe-coupled configuration improved charging and discharging performance compared with the three-fin heat sink.
